text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those findings of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis suggest significant respiratory compromise; what was the appearance of the amniotic fluid, and did you experience any fever or seizures after birth? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Glucose; REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal blood glucose rules out hypoglycemia, and the cyanosis with retractions and nasal flaring indicates significant airway obstruction or lung pathology. Did you have a history of meconium-stained amniotic fluid during birth, and do you have a family history of cystic fibrosis? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5; Chest_X-Ray: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the arterial blood gas showing respiratory acidosis and the chest X-ray revealing ground-glass opacities with air bronchograms, the clinical picture is strongly indicative of Respiratory Distress Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).
